purpose: Screen structurally important directed roads using bridges, edge betweenness and explicit weighted global-efficiency loss.

execution_tiers.name: Weighted topology criticality
execution_tiers.claim: Road ranking by relative weighted global-efficiency loss after removing one uploaded directed road

execution_tiers.name: Demand-weighted road criticality
execution_tiers.claim: Demand-weighted disruption importance; not claimed by the base topology tier

mathematical_formulation.weighted_global_efficiency: mean of reciprocal directed shortest-path impedance over ordered reachable node pairs
mathematical_formulation.ranking: descending road_loss with deterministic identifier tie-breaking

primary_sources.citation: Tarjan, R. (1972). Depth-first search and linear graph algorithms. SIAM Journal on Computing, 1(2), 146-160.
primary_sources.relationship: Supports bridge and connectivity evidence used as visible structural diagnostics.

primary_sources.citation: Latora, V. and Marchiori, M. (2001). Efficient behavior of small-world networks. Physical Review Letters, 87, 198701.
Jenelius, E., Petersen, T. and Mattsson, L.-G. (2006). Importance and exposure in road network vulnerability analysis. Transportation Research Part A, 40(7), 537-560.
primary_sources.relationship: Supports link-removal vulnerability interpretation and the distinction between structural and demand-weighted importance.

verification_contract: Every ranked road is an uploaded directed From-To record
All shortest-path impedances are finite and positive
Reported road loss equals an independent baseline-minus-removal recomputation
Bridge and betweenness evidence do not enter an undisclosed weighted score
known_limitations: The base tier is structural and does not measure observed demand, affected population or evacuation impact
A directed road record is not automatically a complete physical road corridor
Large networks use a disclosed deterministic candidate screen before exact removal tests
